PullRequest.Title: agentHost: wait for client tool result confirmation
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fix the provider-routing bug exposed by the Copilot E2E test `client tool result confirmation is required before the provider continues`.

The protocol state correctly entered pending result confirmation, but the host immediately forwarded the result to the provider. The E2E assertion raced the provider's next model request. Withhold pending results, forward the stored result after approval, and return a failure without the denied content after denial. Apply the same behavior to client-dispatched and server-origin actions.

Add eight deterministic regression cases covering approval and denial on default and peer chats from both action origins, including duplicate completions while confirmation is pending. The existing E2E test and replay fixture are unchanged; no retries, timeout increases, or assertion relaxations.

No separate tracking issue. Reviewed by an Opus 5.5 subagent with no actionable findings. The branch incorporates current `main`.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed, including after integrating `main`.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 289 tests, including after integrating `main`. All eight new cases failed before the fix.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'client tool result confirmation is required' --reporter dot` — passed in 10 consecutive strict-replay runs before integrating `main`.
- `npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 2 --grep 'client tool|client tool-search|client transfers duplicate tool ownership'` — passed, 17 tests and one existing skip, including after integrating `main`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed, including after integrating `main`.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentSideEffects.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts` — passed, including after integrating `main`.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 2` — Copilot, Claude, Copilot OTel, and managed-settings suites passed. Conformance failed on automation operations after restart; Codex failed on a five-second subscribe timeout.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/conformance/agentHostConformance.integrationTest.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/codexAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'a created automation survives an agent host restart|completed file edit remains paired with its result after resume' --reporter dot` — both full-suite failures passed in isolation.

All current-head GitHub Actions workflows passed, including full Agent Host E2E steps on Windows, Linux, and macOS. Pipeline 111 builds [485889](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485889) and [485894](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485894) both succeeded, including two clean Agent Host E2E executions on each of Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64. Both Azure builds disable publishing and release. Copilot review reported no open issues.

(Written by Copilot)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A client tool result that required user confirmation was immediately delivered to the provider, resolving its pending tool handler and starting a continuation model request before approval; denied results could therefore consume provider/network work that should never have started.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: An extra continuation model request and associated model inference/network latency could run while the UI was still waiting for result approval, and become entirely wasted when the user denied the result.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed helper reads the reduced tool-call state, suppresses provider notification while status is PendingResultConfirmation, and forwards exactly once after approval or denial. This removes the eager provider continuation/model-network request from the user-confirmation wait path and also suppresses duplicate completion notifications during that wait.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, every server-origin ChatToolCallComplete reached _notifyClientToolCallComplete at line 485, which immediately called agent.onClientToolCallComplete and resolved the provider's parked client-tool handler. The Copilot implementation routes that result into the pending SDK tool call, allowing the provider to issue its continuation model request. The existing E2E scenario records model request bodies and establishes that the old call occurred while the tool state was still PendingResultConfirmation; the changed guard at line 1615 now returns while that state is pending and the new ChatToolCallResultConfirmed route resumes only after a decision.

Scenarios.Scenario: A client- or server-origin client-tool result requiring confirmation arrives on a default or peer chat and is later approved.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action is reduced into the active turn, the changed helper synchronously looks up the tool call and returns while it is PendingResultConfirmation. Progress intentionally waits on the user's confirmation. The confirmation action is then reduced, the helper looks up the completed tool call, and the provider callback resolves the parked tool handler; the provider's continuation/model request is downstream of approval rather than completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the provider's parked client-tool handler, allowing the provider to issue the continuation model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider continuation per approved tool call after protocol-state deduplication; the pending completion produces zero, and duplicate completions while pending also produce zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary ran immediately for ChatToolCallComplete, before approval, so the continuation model request could start while confirmation was pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After approval this boundary is required for the agent turn to continue; while approval is pending it is intentionally absent from the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: AgentHostStateManager client/server action dispatch reached from agentSideEffects.ts:2073 and the constructor envelope observer at line 478
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish completion and confirmation protocol actions to subscribed clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing protocol publication per dispatched action; default versus peer routing does not fan out provider completion calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both action types were already reduced and published; only provider notification timing changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The completion publication exposes the pending prompt, and confirmation publication precedes/coordinates continuation; the diff does not add another publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One helper invocation per completion and per confirmation. Each invocation searches the active turn's responseParts linearly; effective cardinality is the number of response parts in that single active turn, not all chats or sessions. The reducer already performs a full responseParts traversal for the same action, so the PR adds one inexpensive in-memory traversal, not extra boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Action reduction and side effects are synchronous for each dispatched action. Each confirmation resolves one pending tool handler; there is no collection-wide Promise.all or aggregate network burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat/tool state and provider sessions are resident in in-memory maps; there is no cold filesystem/network cache lookup. Missing chats, turns, or providers terminate without boundary work. Pending confirmations act as the authoritative coalescing state and suppress duplicate completions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reducer ordering, active-turn lookup, provider callback implementations, and the E2E model-request counter directly establish the changed critical path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Turns with unusually many response parts pay an added linear lookup, but realistic tool-call cardinality is bounded by a model turn/context and the scan is small relative to the intentionally deferred model request. No evidence supports user-visible CPU impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes eager model/network work before approval and preserves one continuation after approval; the added in-memory lookup is not a material performance cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: A result requiring confirmation is denied, for client- or server-origin actions on default or peer chats.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion is reduced and withheld. On denial, the reducer changes the tool call to ResultDenied cancellation, the helper creates a small failure result without denied content, and the provider callback resolves the parked tool handler so the turn can handle the failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the provider with a synthetic denial failure, which may lead to one continuation model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one continuation per denied tool call; pending and duplicate completion actions do not cross the provider boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider had already been resumed with the successful/denied content at completion time, before the denial; the denial action itself did not add a second provider call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only after the user decision and is required to unblock the parked provider tool call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One state lookup and one small failure object per denied tool call; denied result content is referenced in protocol state but is not copied into the provider failure.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous decision action resolves one parked call. Independent chats can progress independently, but this diff adds no shared fan-out or unbounded scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache. The active-turn state is the coalescing authority; absent or nonmatching state suppresses forwarding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reducer cancellation state and all three provider callback implementations were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider behavior after receiving a failure varies, but the changed timing and one-call cardinality are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Boundary cardinality remains one but moves after the user decision, avoiding speculative provider work and avoiding serialization of denied content into the provider continuation.

Scenarios.Scenario: A normal client-tool completion does not require result confirmation, including duplicate or stale completion actions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing reducer traversal, the changed helper performs a second active-turn responseParts lookup, then immediately invokes the same provider callback as before. A stale completion whose authoritative state is already Completed may still be forwarded as before, while duplicates arriving during PendingResultConfirmation are newly suppressed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the provider tool handler and permit its continuation request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback per accepted normal completion action, unchanged from before; no loop or chat-wide fan-out is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The completion directly used action.result and invoked the same provider callback without the additional responseParts lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the provider turn to continue; the new state scan is synchronous but only over one active turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added CPU work is O(responseParts in the active turn) per tool completion. It neither clones result content nor scans historical turns, sessions, or chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-action synchronous execution; downstream provider work is controlled by each provider's pending-call map/deferred, not launched in a collection burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resident in-memory state only. Provider/session map misses stop immediately; no retries or negative-cache changes occur.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra scan and unchanged boundary count; low evidence of meaningful magnitude, so it is not reportable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large synthetic turns increase scan cost, but no realistic cardinality or measured duration makes this additional single array scan user-visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. The only added cost is a bounded in-memory lookup alongside an existing reducer-wide traversal, with unchanged I/O/network cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced client/server completion and confirmation paths across default and peer chats. No diff-introduced actionable performance issue was found. The PR instead fixes eager provider continuation/model-network work before result approval; that regression fix was recorded against its introducing commit.
